To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the labour market regulations of low- and mid-income countries are associated with population health, and that a labour market taxonomy of these countries can be used to understand their health.

labour market inequality and labour market poverty are associated with adult mortality, infant mortality, and maternal mortality in low-income countries and that labour market inequality, but not labour market poverty, is associated with adult mortality and infant mortality in middle-income countries.

labour market regulations are an important social determinant of health and that the labour market conditions of LMICs are heterogeneous, which is important to consider for health promotion and disease prevention.
